notes: One-time read-only body-unit check, done once per vehicle per installation (a parked stage of up to two minutes at the start of a session, or a few requests a minute while driving). The units are the body ECUs that answered 19 02 in Car Scanner's log (700 instrument cluster, 701 body controller) and three that commonly sit on the same bus (703 head unit, 705 climate, 750 ESP); none of them is in the OBD probe, so all are marked unprobed. Per unit the app sets the receive address (ATCRA, response id = request id + 8) and flow control, sends 19 02 FF (stored fault codes; also proves the setup works) and service 22 for F180-F1FF, and 10 01 (default session; it makes the unit start its default session afresh, so it is sent only once, after a plain 22 was refused)  (the standard identification identifiers); v1 also asked the instrument cluster 0100-01FF and DD00-DDFF: on 2026-11-24 it answered only 13 identification identifiers (F181 ... F19D) and refused the other 627, none of them the odometer. v2 (this id) asks the cluster only identifiers v1 did not: F400-F4FF (the OBD PID mirror, F4A6 being the odometer), D000-D1FF, 0200-02FF, 1000-10FF and 2000-20FF (1536 in all, the most likely first), still with service 22 only and in the default session (the read-only policy allows no other session). Progress of the other units is carried over from v1 ('continues'): a unit whose identifier count is unchanged keeps its progress, the cluster starts afresh on the new set. Looking for odometer, distance to empty and the cluster's own fuel value; the engine ECU's identifiers are already polled. Answers appear in the recording as 22 xxxx requests to 700-750 and their 62 replies; refusals are expected for most. Runs only on a vehicle whose VIN starts with one of appliesTo (the Tata manufacturer code MAT, as in the Harrier definition). Delete this file once the answer is known.
